attacks.claim: The store and privacy copy says no name is stored, but sync.meta carries a user-set device name that can contain a real name. The published data claim would be inaccurate as written.
attacks.evidence: "sync.meta sidecar (slot, playtime, last-modified, device name)" vs "No email, name, payment or friends data."

attacks.claim: The 1.3 rollback is tested only on the Steam beta branch, yet the plan restores 1.3 as default on both stores. No Epic 1.3 test row exists.
attacks.evidence: "Downgrade to 1.3 (Steam beta branch `1.3-legacy`)" and "1.3 is restored as the default branch on both stores" (ABSENT: Epic 1.3 test row)

attacks.claim: A save written by 1.3 after moving back does not update the sidecar, and the artifact defines no reconciliation when 1.4 sync resumes. This can silently diverge from the server copy, which threatens the never-lose-a-save invariant.
attacks.evidence: "1.3 ignores the sidecar, so a player moved back to 1.3 keeps a working save." and "Server copies and links are kept so sync resumes when re-enabled." (ABSENT: reconciliation rule)

attacks.claim: QA ran on a private Steam branch build and an Epic dev-sandbox build, not the public release binaries, so the pass results do not establish what ships.
attacks.evidence: "Steam build 18204411 on a private branch, Epic build 1.4.0-cl5521 on the Epic dev sandbox" vs "pointed at the production Cross-Save backend with the production config."

attacks.claim: The kill switch is the main emergency control, but the client default when the config fetch fails, and the handling of a cached enabled state, are not defined. An offline or cached client may keep syncing after the flag is flipped.
attacks.evidence: "Kill switch `cross_save_enabled=false` (server config, read on launch and every 10 min)" (ABSENT: default when fetch fails)

attacks.claim: The budget hard stop is said to flip the kill switch automatically, but the mechanism is not described and no QA row tests it. If it fires, sync stops for all players while the UI still reassures them that their saves are safe.
attacks.evidence: "at the stop, the kill switch below is flipped automatically." (ABSENT: mechanism and test)

attacks.claim: The artifact promises every replaced version is kept, but the server caps history at 5 versions and the client at 3, and it does not say which version is pruned first or whether pruned copies are preserved before deletion. Repeated conflicts could remove the only good copy.
attacks.evidence: "Every replaced version is kept: the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot, and the game keeps the last 3 locally in `saves/backup/`."

attacks.claim: 'Newer' is undefined. The artifact does not say whether server clock, device clock, or the device-written sidecar decides the automatic cloud download, so clock skew could make an older save win silently.
attacks.evidence: "On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older." (ABSENT: clock source and skew handling)

attacks.claim: Age gating covers only Epic cabined accounts. The artifact gives no age control or consent basis for Steam accounts, so minors could link and upload cloud saves on Steam.
attacks.evidence: "Epic under-13 (cabined) accounts get a restricted status from EOS; for them linking is not offered" (ABSENT: Steam age gate or consent basis)

attacks.claim: The 'no lost saves' result rests on about 2,450 beta players over two weeks with 11 conflicts. That sample cannot bound a rare data-loss event across 182k players, yet it is presented as settled.
attacks.evidence: "0 lost saves; 11 conflict prompts, all resolved by players."

attacks.claim: Unlink and link creation have no re-authentication or notification. Two live sessions are required, which limits takeover, but a hijacked link cannot be detected or recovered by the victim.
attacks.evidence: "Linking requires valid sessions from both stores at the same time." (ABSENT: unlink re-auth and link-creation notice)

attacks.claim: The load test is a single 30k-concurrent, 10-minute run. It does not cover 503 retry storms or a mass first sync with the 60-uploads/hour cap on patch day.
attacks.evidence: "Load test: 30k concurrent launches syncing in 10 min | p95 410 ms, 0 errors"

attacks.claim: The $3/month storage forecast omits its assumptions. Full quota at the stated per-slot and version sizes is far higher, and the egress figure has no request basis.
attacks.evidence: "forecast ~140 GB at 60% opt-in, about $3/month. Requests and egress ~$90/month."

attacks.claim: 'Your saves on this PC stay where they are' can mislead once a first link uploads data or a conflict prompt changes the active copy. The conflict prompt also does not say the discarded copy is kept in backups.
attacks.evidence: "Your saves on this PC stay where they are." and "Keep the save on this PC (12 h 41 m, today 18:02) or the cloud save (13 h 05 m, today 21:40)?"

attacks.claim: Alerts fire only on sync error rate over 15 minutes, with no alert on checksum rejections or version mismatches, which are the direct signals that the save-integrity invariant is breaking.
attacks.evidence: "Alerts: sync error rate > 2% for 15 min, API 5xx > 1%"

attacks.claim: Linked identity and cloud copies depend on Steam and EOS APIs and a single Frankfurt backend, with no written exit or migration plan. This is a normal platform dependency but unrecorded.
attacks.evidence: "Storage region: EU (Frankfurt) for all players." (ABSENT: exit or migration plan)
